about: A Zork II style underground cavern complex: a barrow, a great cavern with a ravine, a disorienting carousel room, a riddle door, a formal garden with a unicorn, and a bucket-and-well puzzle. The goal seems to be going deeper by solving puzzles.

done.why: I poured water into the bucket while I wasn't in it. It rose and never came back. Every other way on was blocked by rockfall, and I couldn't work out the etchings.

moments.note: The riddle door opened when I answered 'well'.
The etchings were a partial ring of letters, and I couldn't tell what they were for.
The wizard appeared in the topiary and vanished.
Pouring water into the empty bucket sent it up without me, and it never came back.
The carousel room sends you to random rooms, so getting back to a specific one took many tries.

wished: Get into the bucket before pouring water, if that is the intended way.
Some hint about whether the bucket comes back.
A way back to the carousel room's riddle exit that doesn't depend on luck.

lines.line: There is a deafening clap of thunder and the stone door quietly swings open to reveal a passageway beyond.
The bucket swiftly rises up, and is gone.
lines.why: This is where I got stuck.

fun.why: Early exploring was fun and the riddle was satisfying, but I got stuck on the bucket and then spent a long time in the random carousel room.

engagement.why: There was a clear goal at first, which faded once the bucket was gone.

difficulty.why: Everything else was blocked and nothing told me how to get the bucket back.

interestingness.why: Familiar Zork II places with some new details, such as the glowing sword and the etchings.

prose.why: Good descriptions, especially the bucket and the rope.
